component.name: FluxDown
component.summary: Multi-protocol download manager, a free IDM alternative

description.p: This is a community package of FluxDown, maintained independently and unaffiliated with the FluxDown project. It repackages the official upstream Linux build (the .deb release) unmodified.

FluxDown is a download manager with a Rust and Tokio engine and a Flutter interface. It splits transfers into segments that are rebalanced at runtime, keeps every byte tracked in SQLite so downloads survive a crash or reboot, and offers a queue, speed limiting and a system tray.

ul.li: HTTP, HTTPS and FTP downloads with dynamic multi-segment acceleration.
BitTorrent (DHT, magnet), eD2K, and HLS / DASH stream capture.
Light and dark themes, and a built-in Model Context Protocol server on the local API port for AI clients.

description.p: Browser integration: the companion userscript (Settings, then Extensions, then Offline Install Packages) works inside the sandbox — it sends links to the app's local listener over loopback, which the network permission shares. The browser-extension path that relies on Native Messaging is not wired up under Flatpak, because a host browser cannot reach the helper binary inside the sandbox.

Permissions: this package keeps a tight sandbox by default — display, GPU, network, notifications, a tray icon, and your Downloads folder. Saving to any other directory goes through the desktop portal's file chooser. To grant a specific folder permanently, run flatpak override --user --filesystem=~/Media com.fluxdown.app, substituting your own path; --filesystem=home grants the whole home directory.
The in-app updater is not usable here: it replaces the application binary in place, which a read-only Flatpak install does not allow. Updates arrive through Flatpak instead.
FluxDown sends anonymous usage analytics by default; you can turn this off in Settings.
